summary: On Thursday, November 12, 2026, Nvidia's board announced CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately, appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones as the company's first board chair.

Directors launched an independent probe after reports that Huang had affairs with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese asset, and a subordinate who reported to him.

Nvidia shares plummeted 10% in premarket trading Thursday, wiping out about $600 billion in market value this week as investors reacted to leadership uncertainty and potential disruption to the AI infrastructure boom.

The company is initiating a search for a permanent CEO considering internal and external candidates, while management confirmed third-quarter fiscal 2027 results will proceed as scheduled on November 17.

Huang's exit leaves the $4 trillion company navigating an extraordinary transition without a clear successor, while analysts warn the departure could lead to increased regulation and political backlash around artificial intelligence.

This incident unfolded amid an ongoing federal security presence, with hundreds of National Guard members deployed across Washington since President Donald Trump assumed direct federal control over the city in August 2025 to reduce crime.

Witness Ryan Dubicki heard "about five bangs" from his nearby apartment, while gym-goer James Spellman saw a member fall inside after shots were fired. Authorities locked down schools and cordoned off the 1500 block of 15th Street Northwest.

The Metropolitan Police Department, assisted by the Federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the FBI, issued a shelter-in-place order for the 1500 block of 15th Street. The suspect remained at large as of Thursday morning.

Located approximately one mile north of the White House, the Logan Circle neighborhood remained under police control as investigators worked to secure the scene. Officials had not yet released information about the suspect's motive or victims' conditions.
title: 5 people are shot in a trendy DC neighborhood, including 1 killed at a gym, a witness says

summary: On Wednesday, November 11, 2026, Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi’s U.S. Senate seat, defeating Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith. This historic victory makes Colom the state’s first Black U.S. senator since the Reconstruction era.

Colom’s campaign strategy centered on cost-of-living issues. By leveraging a viral ad mocking beef price comments that reached over 6.3 million views, he successfully capitalized on economic discontent within Mississippi.
Official tallies showed Colom leading Hyde-Smith by 4,669 votes after county officials spent over a week processing affidavit ballots. With 99% of ballots reported, Colom secured 49.2% of the vote.

This result brings the Democratic Senate majority to 55 seats, marking the eighth flip of the 2026 cycle. Hyde-Smith posted, "I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," as she congratulated Colom.

The win signals potential shifts in Deep South politics . Colom is scheduled to take office when the new Congress convenes in January 2027, as the first Black senator representing Mississippi since 1881.
title: Scott Colom Flips Mississippi Senate Seat After Weeklong Provisional Ballot Review

Scharf argued that Congress can only investigate matters serving a legislative purpose, claiming Democratic probes are designed to harass and aggrandize rather than advance legitimate ends. Democrats have expressed interest in investigating Donald Trump's real estate projects and crypto dealings.

NYU law professor Ryan Goodman suggested the letter itself may trigger law on obstructing Congress, calling the move "legally repulsive." Washington TV anchor Adam Longo described the warning as "a seismic development."

Garcia responded that "it appears Donald Trump has something to hide," stressing that Congress does not need the permission of the White House to conduct oversight. He previously warned Trump officials to "lawyer up."

Attorney General Todd Blanche said Sunday that "there could be" a crime if rhetoric from Democrats turned threatening, though he emphasized the Department of Justice will continue working with Congress to address questions.
title: White House confronts Democrats over planned probes, claiming they may be ‘blatant criminality’

summary: On Tuesday, the Republican-led House voted 211–204 to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively halting the removal effort during the lame-duck session.

Massie reintroduced the 34-page resolution on Monday, alleging Hegseth violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution regarding military operations in Iran and Yemen and oversaw the unauthorized capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

Hegseth dismissed the resolution as a "farce" and "political spectacle" during a Pentagon briefing, while President Donald Trump praised Hegseth on Truth Social, calling the outcome an "exoneration" of a "Great American Patriot."

Eleven Democrats missed the crucial vote, preventing the opposition from defeating the procedural move; Democratic leaders signaled they may revive impeachment when they take control of Congress in January.

Incoming House Armed Services Committee chair Adam Smith and other Democrats plan to prioritize subpoenaing Hegseth when the new Congress convenes on January 3, signaling a shift toward aggressive investigative oversight.
title: GOP House rejects Hegseth impeachment effort

summary: Senate Republicans reelected Majority Leader John Thune as their leader on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, despite internal pushback following widespread midterm losses.
Widespread election defeats that cost Republicans the Senate majority prompted a day of internal reckoning on Capitol Hill as lawmakers grappled with the party's direction.

The Senate held tense closed-door meetings over whether to delay leadership votes, while the House GOP leadership contest opened between Majority Leader Steve Scalise and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan.

Republican lawmakers expressed deep frustrations over the election performance, with Rep Nathaniel Moran, R-Texas, calling the closed-door meeting a "needed family discussion" to reevaluate the party's path forward.
Members aim to define their legislative agenda for the 120th Congress against incoming Democrats after what Thune described as a "tough night" in the midterm elections.
title: Senate Republicans vote to keep Thune as leader after steep election losses

summary: Existing home sales fell 5.5% last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units, the National Association of Realtors said Thursday, marking the slowest annual sales pace in more than 16 years.
Rising mortgage rates have stifled activity since the war involving Iran began in late February; the 30-year mortgage rate reached 7.4% last month, its highest level in nearly three years.
Sales sank 8.8% compared with last year, falling short of the 3.8 million pace FactSet expected, while median sales price rose 0.4% to $416,700, an all-time high for October.

NAR's chief economist Lawrence Yun said "it is just a tough market for buyers and sellers," as the housing market remains in a slump that began in 2022 when mortgage rates climbed from pandemic-era lows.
Traditionally, a 4- to 6-month supply signals a balanced market, but inventory rose 1.3% last month to represent a 5.1-months' supply, the largest since November 2015.
title: US existing home sales slump to more than 16-year low in October

summary: On Monday, November 9, 2026, Anchorage Police Department officers arrested Jack Sabato, 32, in connection with a fatal hit-and-run crash that killed 42-year-old Carl Simmonds near Airport Heights Drive and DeBarr Road.

Surveillance footage from the Blood Bank of Alaska identified the white Chevrolet Tahoe, which police later located at an Amazon warehouse with fresh damage to the right front corner consistent with a pedestrian strike.

According to charging documents, Sabato told officers he was 'doing late night DoorDashing' when 'something' suddenly appeared in the road; he acknowledged hitting 'something' but did not stop due to fear of lacking insurance.

Arraigned on Tuesday at Anchorage Jail Courtroom, Sabato was held at the Anchorage Correctional Complex with bail set at $5,000; his father, Antonio Sabato Jr., requested privacy for the family amid the crisis.

Simmonds is the ninth pedestrian killed by a vehicle in Anchorage this year, as Sabato faces felony charges of leaving the scene of an accident without assisting the injured and related misdemeanor charges.
title: Son of Virginia Madsen, Antonio Sabàto Jr. Arrested After Fatal Hit-and-Run

summary: On Thursday, the US Department of Labor reported initial jobless claims increased by 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 200,000 for the week ending November 7, exceeding the 195,000 economists had forecast.
Despite the recent uptick, jobless claims remained at levels consistent with a resilient labor market, with applications holding at or below 200,000 for nine straight weeks across the United States.
Continuing claims, a proxy for hiring, fell by 20,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.697 million for the week ended October 31, tracking individuals remaining on benefits beyond their initial week.

Citigroup economist Veronica Clark suggested a smaller workforce could reduce unemployment filings, while benefit exhaustion limited to a "maximum of 26 weeks" in most states may also restrain continuing claims.

Projections indicate the unemployment rate could move closer to 4.0% by early 2027, assuming continuing claims remain at levels supporting a stable labor market despite potential workforce contractions.
title: US jobless claims tick up to 200,000 but remain low by historic standards

Hokit sparked controversy in June by shouting "Man" to label Michelle Obama at a UFC event on the White House South Lawn marking President Donald Trump's birthday celebration.

President Donald Trump offered UFC chief Dana White the position of White House press secretary over the weekend; White declined the frivolous offer following the organization's event.

With a 10-0 record, Hokit challenges Gane for the heavyweight belt at Saturday's main event at Madison Square Garden, after Gane was elevated following former interim champion Tom Aspinall's eye injury.

Following credible intelligence warnings of potential Iranian attacks, the military increased security to Force Protection Condition Charlie at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath, relocating aircraft including Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers and three Osprey aircraft.

These UK-based installations support more than 5,000 active-duty American military personnel; Downing Street said the safety of British airbases was a "top priority" as officials moved assets following the threat assessment.
In an interview with Al Mayadeen TV, Rezaei claimed Iran will not allow a "single speck" of enriched uranium to leave the country, rejecting American demands for a political settlement.

President Donald Trump characterized the war as "militarily over" and said future strikes are "unlikely," yet Iran continues expanding missile production to about 50 monthly, complicating de-escalation efforts.
title: Iran Warns It Will Target US Bases in Europe After Any New Attack

summary: On Wednesday, the Wisconsin Supreme Court voted 5-1 to hear a lawsuit challenging Act 10, the 2011 law that stripped most public employees of collective bargaining rights.
Dane County Circuit Court Judge Jacob Frost ruled the law unconstitutional in December 2024, finding no rational basis for treating public safety employees differently than general workers.

The Wisconsin 2nd District Court of Appeals reversed Frost's decision in July, yet Justice Brian Hagedorn recused himself from the Supreme Court proceedings due to his prior role as Scott Walker's chief legal counsel.
Democrats' recent electoral victories have given the party control of state government, with many incoming officials on record supporting repeal of the law.
Unions argue the law's classification of general employees lacks rational basis, as the category includes Capitol Police and conservation wardens denied rights afforded police and firefighters.
title: Wisconsin Supreme Court says it will hear Act 10 case

summary: On Wednesday, former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to the Metro Nashville Police Department facing six misdemeanor warrants stemming from an incident involving two pedestrians last Thursday.

According to the Metro Nashville Police Department, the 63-year-old was driving his truck just before midnight last Thursday at Fourth Avenue and Broadway when he made a right turn, running over the feet of two pedestrians.

Police allege Ryan drove away after the collision, though pedestrians photographed his license plate. He faces two counts each of leaving the scene of an accident, failing to render aid, and disobeying traffic signals.
A judicial commissioner set Ryan's bond at $6,000. ESPN issued a statement: "We are aware and are in touch with Rex," regarding the charges against their analyst.

Ryan, a former New York Jets coach and ESPN analyst, is a self-proclaimed "toe expert." Critics noted the irony: "if anyone should have checked on someone's feet after being run over by a truck, then it should have been him.
title: Former NFL Coach Rex Ryan Turns Himself in After Alleged Nashville Hit-and-Run Injured 2 Pedestrians, Police Say

Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to focus "his complete and total attention" on crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities, prioritizing this domestic effort over pursuing formal negotiations with Iran.

The administration claims the federal Budget could be quickly BALANCED by correcting large-scale criminal activity within Democrat Leadership, presenting this approach as superior to diplomatic efforts involving the Strait.

title: Trump says ‘we don’t need a deal with Iran’

A caravan of roughly 1,000 migrants entered southern Mexico on Nov. 6, according to Latin Times; Mexican authorities blocked a separate group of about 100 migrants on Nov. 10 as groups began an illegal march.
Declaring "There will be no leniency," Trump alleged some travelers are individuals whom other countries do not want and are being sent to the United States.
Trump informed the Border Patrol, ICE, and Customs Enforcement of his position, stating migrants would not be accepted into the United States while criticizing the Texas governor as "very liberal."
Immigration remains central to Republican strategy as Trump linked the caravan movement to his party's perceived loss in last week's midterms, suggesting continued border focus ahead.
title: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not halt migrants

summary: On Wednesday, a Dallas County jury convicted rapper Yella Beezy, legally Markies Conway, of capital murder in the 2020 killing of rival rapper Mo3, whose real name was Melvin Noble.
Prosecutors argued Conway orchestrated the shooting as part of a long-running feud between the two artists, alleging he paid gunman Kewon White $40,000 to carry out the murder.
Evidence presented showed White wore a mask and fired over 40 rounds from an AK-47-style pistol on Interstate 35, killing Noble while a bystander survived the November 2020 attack.
Following the guilty verdict, Conway received a life sentence without the possibility of parole, joining gunman White, who was previously convicted and sentenced to life for his role.
Another defendant, Devin Brown, is scheduled to stand trial later this year for his alleged connection to the murder plot, keeping the case active.
title: Rapper Yella Beezy convicted of hiring gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 on busy Dallas interstate

Stability in China-US relations is "a rational choice made by the two major countries based on respective and shared interests," Minister Wang said. Trump-Xi summits this year helped stabilize ties despite unresolved disputes.
Rubio said on Nov 10 that work is underway to arrange a trilateral meeting involving Donald Trump , Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the APEC Economic Leaders Meeting sidelines.

On Nov 8, Trump stated he expects to discuss ending wars in Iran and denuclearization at the Shenzhen summit, while reports suggest Putin may pitch discussions on Russia's long-running war in Ukraine.

The APEC Economic Leaders Meeting approaches as negotiators work to finalize the trilateral summit. China previously rejected trilateral nuclear disarmament talks as unrealistic, though the gathering may facilitate broader strategic dialogue.
title: US Says China Agreed Importance of Leader-Level Talks to Advance Denuclearisation

summary: Mexico 's federal Protection Mechanism for Human Rights Defenders and Journalists, created in 2012 to safeguard threatened reporters, faces scrutiny for failing to prevent attacks; critics estimate 98% of journalist homicides remain unpunished.

Journalist Alberto Amaro endured over 30 violent encounters, including gunfire and death threats linked to his reporting on police and organized crime in Tlaxcala; after waiting more than 48 hours for a federal response following a shooting, he turned to courts for emergency security.

Priscila Pacheco, daughter of slain journalist Francisco Pacheco, faces unreliable security measures while working for the state-level Protection Mechanism; she reports that authorities denied her personal protection and failed to maintain critical equipment like panic buttons and home security systems.

After three years displaced from Iguala, Guerrero, Jonathan Cuevas returned following a truce between criminal groups; however, he received new death threats, illustrating the Mechanism's inability to coordinate with federal prosecutors or provide effective long-term safety.

While President Claudia Sheinbaum promised additional Protection Mechanism funding in 2025, Reporters Without Borders reports little progress on press freedom commitments; the Inter-American Commission for Human Rights emphasizes the state must shift from reactive investigation to active attack prevention.
title: Mexico's Journalist Protection Mechanism Leaves Reporters Vulnerable

Center and right perspectives present a more qualified interpretation: they emphasize “routine” testing while stressing that “possible benefits now outweigh potential harms,” with center coverage detailing biennial tests for average-risk men 50–69 and annual screening from 45 for high-risk men.

The pivotal divide is urgency versus risk-benefit context, though all agree the guidelines now support broader PSA screening because medical advances and accumulating evidence have shifted the balance.
summary: On Thursday, the American Cancer Society recommended that men ages 50 to 69 at average risk undergo prostate-specific antigen blood level screening every two years, replacing previous discretionary guidance.

A major European randomized study with over two decades of follow-up found routine testing significantly lowers prostate cancer deaths, prompting the ACS to shift from the flexible, discretionary advice in previous 2010 guidelines.

Annual screening at 45 is advised for high-risk groups, including Black men and those with family history. To reduce unnecessary biopsies, the ACS now suggests MRIs or biomarker tests after elevated readings, with 3.0 nanograms/milliliter set as the high-level threshold.

James Eastham, chief of urology at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, called the update "a balanced approach" that helps physicians refer patients earlier. Survivor Eddie Baynes said the guidelines "hit the nail on the head."

Guidelines emphasize active surveillance for slow-growing tumors to prevent overtreatment. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, which currently recommends against routine screening, announced an upcoming update to its own guidelines.
title: American Cancer Society calls for routine prostate cancer screening in guideline change

Center coverage de-emphasizes partisan accountability in favor of location, responder scale, and the investigation.
The pivotal divide is whether adjacent construction is chiefly a question of accountability or documented inquiry.

All perspectives stress fatalities, injuries, rubble, rescue workers, and uncertainty over totals, reflecting shared concern shaped by broader debates over safety, regulation, and institutional responsibility.
summary: At least eight people died after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in Brooklyn, New York.
At least 17 people were injured, including three firefighters, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
Emergency crews continued searching through the rubble for people who may still be trapped beneath the wreckage.
Firefighters and police officers worked overnight using pickaxes and power saws to rescue survivors and recover victims.
title: Death toll rises to 8 in Brooklyn building collapse as rescuers dig through rubble

bias: The coverage shows little genuine left-right ideological conflict; its differences are mainly commercial and national framing.

The left-leaning headline uses promotional terms such as “launch,” “first,” and “weakness pills,” while emphasizing China’s importance as the world’s second-largest pharmaceutical market and Eli Lilly ’s “advantage” over Novo Nordisk.

Right-Leaning coverage highlights a U.S. pharmaceutical company, calls the result a “lead,” and presents the pill as an “alternative” to injections—commercially favorable language, not clear conservative rhetoric.
Center coverage names orforglipron and China’s regulator.
Across perspectives, approval, first-mover status, competitive advantage, and pill-versus-injection convenience remain shared themes.
summary: On Nov 12, 2026, Eli Lilly received regulatory approval in China for a GLP-1 weight-loss pill, becoming the first company to gain this approval in the world's second-largest pharmaceutical market.
Rising obesity rates in China prompted regulatory interest; the National Health Commission projects overweight or obese populations could reach more than 65% by 2030, up from roughly 50% in 2020.
Lilly will compete against once-weekly GLP-1 injections from Novo Nordisk, Pfizer, and Innovent Biologics, though oral therapies may attract patients reluctant to use needles.
Novo has also submitted an application to sell its oral Wegovy pill in China, though approval remains pending while the company trails Lilly in securing market entry.
Yang Huang, head of China healthcare research at Morgan, forecasts annual GLP-1 sales could reach 30 billion yuan within the next five to seven years, up from 3 billion to 4 billion yuan currently.
title: Eli Lilly becomes first drugmaker to have a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Chinese firms’ overseas Nvidia scramble as a response to U.S. “curbs,” “restraints,” and an alleged “ technology block,” emphasizing vulnerability and the disputed personal-espionage controversy around Jensen Huang.

Right-Leaning accounts heighten geopolitical alarm, describing “panic,” “spy” claims, and Beijing’s charge that Washington “fabricates spy stories,” portraying China’s reaction as evidence of a security confrontation.
Center coverage treats the rush as a market-and-policy issue, stressing a possible regulatory “gap” and legislation governing cloud access.

All perspectives highlight overseas computing demand, potential restrictions, and intensifying U.S.-China technology rivalry, differing mainly over coercion, credibility, and national-security implications.
summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are seeking to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at overseas data centers, fearing a scandal involving CEO Jensen Huang could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on remote access to advanced processors.

The Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would grant the Commerce Department authority to regulate cloud-based access to restricted technology; the House passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and companies worry controversy surrounding Huang will accelerate its passage.

Procurement records show a Chinese university with ties to the Liberation Army recently obtained powerful H200 AI chips despite U.S. export restrictions, exposing enforcement gaps that companies now fear will be closed.

Smaller AI labs are approaching computing providers in Southeast Asia to secure capacity before potential new regulations eliminate their ability to rent remote computing power without importing restricted chips directly.

On Sunday, Huang admitted to infidelity, prompting companies to accelerate risk mitigation as remote access remains vital for China's developers to train large AI models without importing restricted chips directly.
title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of US curbs: Reuters

bias: Left-Leaning coverage portrays Florida’s measure as an “anti-DEI crusade” that “backfires,” “sweeps up” a beloved, nearly six-decade-old parade , and fuels “outrage,” while scrutinizing the mayor’s “silence” on Pride and alleged selective concern.
Right-Leaning coverage instead says the law is “blocking” both events, emphasizing governmental restriction without dwelling on the mayor or public anger.
Center coverage de-emphasizes partisan rhetoric, detailing CS/CS/SB 1134, its January 1, 2027 effective date, and the city’s legal interpretation.

The pivotal divide is whether this is ideological overreach and unequal priorities or statutory compliance; all acknowledge both cancellations and the clash between Florida’s DEI politics and local cultural autonomy.
summary: On Tuesday, Delray Beach officials announced they will not host the city's annual St. Patrick's Day or Pride events in 2027, citing a new Florida law banning municipal funding or promotion of diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.

Senate Bill 1134, signed by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis in April, prohibits local governments from funding or promoting activities referenced by ethnicity, sexual orientation, or gender identity starting January 1, 2027.

Dating back to 1968, the St. Patrick's Day parade has grown into "one of South Florida's largest annual" events, triggering significant backlash from residents on social media following the announcement.
Delray Beach Mayor Tom Carney, a Republican, vowed to fight for the parade's survival, while City Manager Terrence Moore said a "private interest" could sponsor the event.
Organizers may still secure permits issued "in a content-neutral manner," as the legislation allows cities to provide public safety services for privately funded gatherings.
title: Florida city says it will not host St Patrick's Day parade, Pride event due to anti-diversity law

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds Huang’s affair and frames Nvidia ’s decline with words like “sinks” and “plummeted,” while de-emphasizing succession.

Right-Leaning coverage intensifies accountability through “hammered,” “in disgrace,” and “forced out,” emphasizing reported Wall Street downgrades and possible internal or external successors—claims not confirmed in the excerpts.
Center coverage broadens the lens with an approximately 11% opening drop, a market value below $4 trillion, family trusts, and a reported—but unverified—Chinese-spy connection.
All sides link the resignation to a sharp share-price fall, but their priorities reflect wider divides over scandal, governance, financial risk, and geopolitical scrutiny.
summary: Nvidia faces unprecedented turbulence after co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a second extramarital affair with an employee. Huang had previously acknowledged being "unfaithful" to his wife, Lori Huang, with a woman intelligence officials believe was a spy for China.

Jensen and Lori Huang jointly own about 800 million Nvidia shares worth roughly $135 billion through a complex web of trusts and LLCs created for tax and estate planning purposes, according to SEC filings.
Lori Huang serves as president of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation, which reported $9 billion in net assets in 2024. She is co-trustee of the trusts holding most of their Nvidia stake.

The CEO's sudden exit combined with affair revelations creates uncertainty for Nvidia's financial future, yet the shared ownership structure makes it difficult for either spouse to quickly liquidate their massive stake.

Experts note the irrevocable trust structure acts as a stabilizing force, as these separate entities are theoretically protected from creditors or divorcing spouses. This arrangement potentially prevents large-scale share liquidation despite the resignation.
title: Nvidia on track to lose more than $700 billion in value as Jensen Huang resigns

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Bikar and Bokak as a “natural paradise” and among the “last wild and healthy ecosystems,” stressing what human activity has “lost,” ecological decline, and the Marshall Islands’ new marine reserve.

Right-Leaning coverage emphasizes discovery and reassurance—“wild and untouched,” “pristine,” and even a “world is still in order”—while spotlighting possible species unknown to science and minimizing policy implications.

Center coverage softens both frames with “remarkably untouched,” study context, and qualifications such as “may be.” The dividing line is whether the atolls primarily symbolize environmental damage or nature’s remaining resilience; all perspectives agree they are exceptionally biodiverse reference points for ecosystems degraded elsewhere.
summary: A new study in Frontiers in Marine Science confirms Bikar Atoll and Bokak Atoll in the Marshall Islands remain "relatively intact" ecosystems, positioning them as vital ecological reference systems amid global biodiversity loss.

Researchers from the University of Hawai'i led a 2023 expedition to survey the remote atolls, which informed the Marshall Islands Government's decision to designate 18,532 square miles as the country's first national marine sanctuary.

The survey documented 266 reef fish taxa and 132 green sea turtle nest pits concentrated at Bikar, while Bokak featured coral-dominated reefs where hard corals and encrusting algae made up 60 to 80 percent of shallow waters.

Sharks accounted for 33.9 percent of fore-reef biomass at Bokak and 26.8 percent at Bikar, demonstrating what marine ecologist Alan Friedlander called an "unparalleled glimpse" into habitats with minimal human influence.

These findings support the Marshall Islands' community-led Reimaanlok vision for protecting marine resources, as Friedlander concluded the government should be applauded for protecting these global biodiversity hotspots where habitats "teem with life.
title: Scientists find some of the 'very last wild and healthy ecosystems' in the world's oceans untouched by humans

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the case primarily as alleged parental criminal abuse, stressing “buried alive,” “survived,” and “attempted murder,” while de-emphasizing the search operation and recovery details.

Right-Leaning coverage heightens moral outrage and astonishment, using “abusive father,” “miraculously,” and “miracle,” and highlighting the air pocket and cool temperatures as possible explanations for survival.

summary: On Tuesday, authorities in Lexington County, South Carolina, rescued 11-month-old Koah Sharp, who was found buried alive in a dog crate; his 25-year-old father, Michael Comer, was charged with attempted murder.

The search began Monday after Koah's grandmother left the infant with Comer, who authorities say vanished with the child; police arrested the father in Batesburg-Leesville, about a 40-minute drive from Columbia.

Nearly 100 first responders searched until they heard the infant's cries from underground; Sheriff Jay Koon said a towel wrapped around the crate created an air pocket, helping Koah survive an estimated 24 hours.

Koah was released from the hospital Tuesday night and is expected to make a full recovery, while Comer remains in custody awaiting a court hearing Thursday for charges including unlawful conduct and burglary.

Authorities haven't revealed a motive for the alleged crime; great-aunt Amber Hammond said the family 'had no idea something like this would happen,' while grandfather John Comer expressed relief at his rescue.
title: Father Charged with Attempted Murder After 11-Month-Old Son Found Buried Alive

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames DeSantis’s warrant as part of a “record-setting pace,” using “scheduled to be killed” and highlighting exonerated prisoners’ calls to “slow” or pause executions, foregrounding wrongful-conviction and death-penalty concerns.

Right-Leaning coverage instead stresses “chilling” circumstances—the child’s disappearance, alleged drugging of her mother, and “condemned killer”—portraying execution as the expected consequence of conviction.
Center coverage is more procedural, emphasizing the warrant, timeline, and victim’s age while retaining some context about a possible pause.

The pivotal divide is whether the story signifies state-sanctioned killing and systemic risk or justice for a horrifying crime ; all emphasize DeSantis’s action, Crain’s conviction, and Florida’s 22nd execution, reflecting broader punishment-versus-due-process divides.
summary: On Tuesday, Governor Ron DeSantis signed a death warrant for Willie Seth Crain, convicted in the 1998 murder of 7-year-old Amanda Brown in Hillsborough County. Crain is scheduled for execution by lethal injection on December 10, 2026, at Florida State Prison in Raiford.

Crain was convicted of kidnapping and murdering Brown after she disappeared in 1998, though her body was never found. Prosecutors secured the conviction using blood evidence discovered in Crain's bathroom and on his clothing.

This warrant marks the 22nd execution in Florida this year, continuing a record-setting pace. Florida has matched its 2025 record of 19 executions, accounting for more than half of all executions in the United States this year combined.
Exonerated former death row inmates are asking Governor-elect Byron Donalds to pause executions. Spiritual advisor Jeff Hood wrote to Donalds, "This pace has to stop," opposing the accelerated pace.

Before Crain's scheduled execution, two other death warrants are pending. Thomas Mitchell Overton is set to be put to death on November 19, and Richardo Gonzalez is scheduled for execution on December 1.
title: DeSantis Signs Death Warrant for Man Convicted in 1998 Murder of 7-Year-Old Girl in Hillsborough County

summary: On Wednesday, Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton called for Israel to allow aid trucks into Gaza, a day after visiting the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.
During his visit to a logistics center, Hamilton observed food trucks regularly held up or facing major delays at the border, with officials rejecting items for "crazy reasons."
The Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram that "Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in," criticizing denial of freedom and dignity in Gaza.
Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide, stating its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants rather than civilians.
The next Formula One race occurs in Las Vegas on 21 Nov, with The Brit currently fourth in the standings before the season concludes in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
title: Lewis Hamilton urges Israel to let Gaza aid in after Rafah visit

summary: On Wednesday, Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the eastern border with Jordan to inspect military posts and a barrier under construction, emphasizing readiness against potential threats.
Zamir toured a sector assigned to the 96th Gilad Regional Division, which monitors the frontier stretching from the Israel-Jordan-Syria tri-border area southward past the Dead Sea.
Calling the Jordan Valley 'Israel's eastern defensive wall,' Zamir described the area as an 'essential component of our national security and strategic depth' amid IDF reinforcements.
The military chief stated forces must be prepared for 'rapid change and surprise,' as the division applies lessons from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack to address infiltration threats.
Accompanied by senior officers including Central Command head Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, Zamir met with leaders of the Jordan Valley Regional Council to strengthen regional security cooperation.
title: IDF Chief Stresses Need for Constant Readiness During Jordan Border Visit

summary: Israeli courts rejected petitions seeking the release of 14 Palestinian doctors from Gaza who are held without charges or trials.
The Lod District Court refused Dr. Hussam Abu Safia’s request for an independent medical examination and a second medical opinion.
Physicians for Human Rights Israel said Abu Safia had lost 14 kilograms, experienced falling hemoglobin levels, and had chest pain that was not properly investigated.
The group said the detentions further weaken Gaza’s healthcare system, which faces a severe shortage of medical workers after widespread infrastructure damage.
title: Israeli Court Refuses to Release 14 Gaza Doctors Held without Charge or Trial

summary: On Tuesday, the FBI added Shahram Poursafi, a member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps , to its Most Wanted Terrorists list for allegedly soliciting the murders of two former U.S. government officials.
Court documents indicate the plot against National Security Advisor John Bolton was intended as retaliation for the January 2020 killing of Qasem Soleimani, commander of the Iranian Quds Force.

The FBI is offering a $20 million reward for information on Poursafi and three associates: Mohammad Reza Ansari, Abolfazl Alizadeh, and Mohammad Hossein Shamoradizadeh, who allegedly "participated in lethal plotting."
Charged in 2022, Poursafi—also known as Mehdi Rezayi—allegedly sought to pay individuals $300,000 for the assassination, according to a Justice Department complaint.

Gregory Heeb of the FBI Washington Field Office's Counterterrorism Division stated the bureau "will not stand for the IRGC's brazen attempts to silence, harm or murder" activists, journalists, and public officials.
title: FBI Adds IRGC Member Shahram Poursafi to Most Wanted Terrorists List

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames SJ Howell’s selection as a milestone, using phrases like “make history,” “well-known trans advocate,” and “ transgender /nonbinary” to foreground representation, while also highlighting Zooey Zephyr’s whip role.

Right-Leaning coverage compresses the event into an identity-centered description—“nonbinary leader”—de-emphasizing the claimed national “first,” advocacy context, and policy implications, without overtly hostile terms like “woke” or “far-left.” Center coverage remains restrained, adding Missoula and attributing the “first” claim to Zephyr.
All perspectives acknowledge Howell’s selection and identity, but diverge over whether the pivotal story is inclusive progress, institutional change, or partisan cultural symbolism.
summary: Montana House Democrats elected State Rep. SJ Howell of Missoula as minority leader on Wednesday, making Howell the first trans/nonbinary party leader in the region.
Before their 2022 election as Montana's first nonbinary legislator, Howell worked as a lobbyist and activist for women's and LGBTQ issues.
Democrats also elected State Rep. Zooey Zephyr of Missoula as a minority whip, following her 2023 remarks that colleagues supporting gender-affirming care bans would have "blood" on their hands.
House Republicans elected Katie Zolnikov of Billings as House speaker, Mike Vinton of Billings as speaker pro tem, and Tom Millett of Marion as majority leader.
The new leadership team announced "we have an incredible leadership team, and are ready to get to work for Montana," signaling a shift in the Legislature's partisan balance.
title: Montana Democrats choose trans/nonbinary person to be state House minority leader
